# Aunt Lavinia

## Overview

- **Age:** at least seventy  <sub>[v1 CHAPTER XIX. A Concert, a Catastrophe, and a Confession P54](../source/v01-c19.md#nw-v01-c19-p0054)</sub>
- **Gender:** female  <sub>[v1 CHAPTER XIX. A Concert, a Catastrophe, and a Confession P58](../source/v01-c19.md#nw-v01-c19-p0058), [v1 CHAPTER XIX. A Concert, a Catastrophe, and a Confession P77](../source/v01-c19.md#nw-v01-c19-p0077)</sub>

- **Titles:** Miss  <sub>[v1 CHAPTER XXXIV. A Regent’s Girl P13](../source/v01-c34.md#nw-v01-c34-p0013)</sub>
- **Family:** [Isolde Pembroke](../character/isolde-pembroke.md) (relative)

## Appearance

Aunt Lavinia is a slender, stern, and unbending woman. She wears gold-rimmed spectacles, behind which her eyes flash when she is angry.

_Sources: [v1 CHAPTER XIX. A Concert, a Catastrophe, and a Confession P77](../source/v01-c19.md#nw-v01-c19-p0077)_

## Personality

Aunt Lavinia is known for being bad-tempered, strict, and proper. Because of her terribly stern demeanor, she is prone to giving terrible scolding over misbehavior.

_Sources: [v1 CHAPTER XIX. A Concert, a Catastrophe, and a Confession P54](../source/v01-c19.md#nw-v01-c19-p0054), [v1 CHAPTER XIX. A Concert, a Catastrophe, and a Confession P58](../source/v01-c19.md#nw-v01-c19-p0058)_

## History

Aunt Lavinia is the wealthy aunt of Isolde's father who resides in [Port Marlow](../codex/places.md#port-marlow) at her home, [Beechwood](../codex/places.md#beechwood). During a visit to the [Pembroke](../character/pembroke.md) home, she was initially furious after [Nell](../character/nell-harcourt.md) and Isolde accidentally jumped into bed on top of her late at night. However, after [Nell](../character/nell-harcourt.md) personally apologized and took full responsibility, Aunt Lavinia forgave the girls and formed a fond friendship with [Nell](../character/nell-harcourt.md). She later hosted the girls at [Beechwood](../codex/places.md#beechwood) for a week, warmly welcoming them to attend the local [Exhibition](../codex/places.md#exhibition) and a concert.

_Sources: [v1 CHAPTER XIX. A Concert, a Catastrophe, and a Confession P9](../source/v01-c19.md#nw-v01-c19-p0009), [v1 CHAPTER XIX. ## Quotes

> "Oh, is that so, hey? It seems to me Isolde performed at least her fair portion of the leaping. Such behavior occurring within an honorable home!"
>
> — Aunt Lavinia — [v1 CHAPTER XIX. A Concert, a Catastrophe, and a Confession P82](../source/v01-c19.md#nw-v01-c19-p0082)

> “My decision is made to remain merely to become more familiar with that Nell-girl,” she admitted openly. “She entertains me, and when one reaches my age, somebody who provides entertainment is uncommon.”
>
> — Aunt Lavinia — [v1 CHAPTER XIX. A Concert, a Catastrophe, and a Confession P92](../source/v01-c19.md#nw-v01-c19-p0092)

> "Bear in mind, you Nell-girl, that you are to pay me a visit when you arrive in town, where I will lodge you in the most unoccupied spare-room bed I have for sleeping."
>
> — Aunt Lavinia — [v1 CHAPTER XIX. A Concert, a Catastrophe, and a Confession P96](../source/v01-c19.md#nw-v01-c19-p0096)

> "Goodness, child, what growth you’ve had! I do declare, you stand taller than me. Furthermore, you are far better-looking than you used to be as well. Though I expect you are already aware of that without anyone telling you."
>
> — Aunt Lavinia — [v1 CHAPTER XXIX. An Epoch in Nell’s Life P18](../source/v01-c29.md#nw-v01-c29-p0018)

> "I suppose I might if you drop by to chat with me every now and then,"
>
> — Aunt Lavinia — [v1 CHAPTER XIX. A Concert, a Catastrophe, and a Confession P90](../source/v01-c19.md#nw-v01-c19-p0090)

### [Isolde Pembroke](../character/isolde-pembroke.md) · [the relationship](../relationships/aunt-lavinia--isolde-pembroke.md)

### [Nell Harcourt](../character/nell-harcourt.md) · [the relationship](../relationships/aunt-lavinia--nell-harcourt.md)

Aunt Lavinia and [Nell](../character/nell-harcourt.md) share a strong friendship that began after a rocky first meeting. After [Nell](../character/nell-harcourt.md) and Isolde accidentally jumped into bed on top of the visiting aunt, Aunt Lavinia was furious and prepared to leave, but [Nell](../character/nell-harcourt.md) took full responsibility and charmed her into staying. Following this reconciliation, Aunt Lavinia welcomed [Nell](../character/nell-harcourt.md) into her home at [Beechwood](../codex/places.md#beechwood) for a week-long visit to enjoy the local [Exhibition](../codex/places.md#exhibition) and concert.

_Sources: [v1 CHAPTER XIX. A Concert, a Catastrophe, and a Confession P9](../source/v01-c19.md#nw-v01-c19-p0009), [v1 CHAPTER XIX.
